events.text: The silver floor holds one throne, and on it sits a ruler in the robes of the house your soul once founded. The face is yours, older and harder. It fought you with a sceptre and an army of silver ghosts, and lost. Now it looks at you over the broken sceptre. "Did they remember me kindly?" it asks.

choices.text: Tell it the truth: they remembered the taxes

effects.log: The old ruler laughs, a short dry sound you recognise as your own. "Good. Then they remembered." It fades into the silver, lighter.

choices.text: Tell it they built shrines to its name

effects.log: It nods slowly, and you see it does not believe you, and is grateful anyway. A small silver seal rolls to your feet.

choices.text: Take the broken sceptre with you

effects.log: You pick up the halves. The ruler watches you go with the look of someone handing over a burden. The silver is cold in your sleeve for the rest of the climb.

events.text: The self on floor {tw_floor} wears black and smiles the way you hoped you never had. It was the worst of your lives, and it is proud of every year. You beat it, but it does not seem to mind. "You still owe for me," it says, and taps the ledger the Tower keeps of your soul. "Will you say you enjoyed none of it?"

choices.text: Admit some of it was easy, and that was the worst part

effects.log: The smile goes out of its face. "Yes," it says quietly. "That was the worst part." It steps aside, and the debt in you feels a little lighter for being named.

choices.text: Say nothing and walk past it

effects.log: It laughs at your back all the way to the stairs. The laugh is still there when you sleep that night.

choices.text: Tell it you will pay what it owes

effects.log: It looks at you a long time. "Nobody ever offered," it says. It hands you a silver coin with your old face on it, and you keep it.

The Tower has shelved a life of yours beside it: the year you stood between it and the hunters. It lost to you today only because it would not truly strike. events.text: The array on floor {tw_floor} copies the laws of a world you made: its heaven, its seasons, its one great rule. You knew the laws, so you passed. But the copy shows a flaw you never saw from above. A small one. The kind that, in a few thousand years, people will pay for.

choices.text: Mend the law in the array, and remember the mend

effects.log: You change one line. The copied world in gold shivers and settles. You will have to make the same change in the real one.

events.text: Floor {tw_floor} is a talisman array missing one character. The rest of the great sheet of gold is written in a master's hand, and in the gap is a brush, still wet. You found the floor's way through. Now the brush waits for the last stroke.

effects.log: The array becomes a door, and stays one. The next climber will thank someone they will never meet.
The whole floor softens. You sit down in it and sleep the best sleep you have had in years.
Your name sits in gold among a master's characters. It looks small. It looks like it belongs.

effects.log: It is strange company and it does not stay long. You are a little less afraid of it after.

events.text: Floor {tw_floor} is a time array. A sign at the door warns that every wrong move costs a year outside. You made four wrong moves before the right one. Nothing seems to have changed. Then you notice the dust on your sleeves, and how long your hair has grown.

choices.text: Count the years and let them go

choices.text: Study the array until you understand the right move

effects.log: You understand it at last, too late to save the years and early enough for every climb after.

events.text: On floor {tw_floor} a round little apprentice of the Golden Abacus challenged you to count faster than a sage: beads, steps, the bells of the eaves. You won by one bead. The apprentice is furious and delighted. "Master Geum-ha will want to hear this," they say. "Nobody beats me."

choices.text: Tell them you cheated by counting bells twice

effects.log: The apprentice stares, then laughs so hard they drop the abacus. "That is the master's trick," they gasp. "He will like you."

choices.text: Ask for a rematch next year

effects.log: "Next year," they agree, and write it down in gold on the back of their hand. They will not forget.

events.text: A war god of the Divine Realm has been stuck on floor {tw_floor} for three hundred years. He beats the array every day with a spear of red light, and every day it grows stronger. His banners are faded. When you walk through the gap you found, he stops mid-swing and stares.

effects.log: He watches you walk it twice. Then he lays down the spear, very carefully, and walks it himself. On the far side he does not thank you. He sits down and weeps like a soldier.

choices.text: Tell him to stop hitting it

effects.log: "Stop?" he says, as if you had said a word in a foreign tongue. He goes on swinging, slower, and watches you go.
His spear stops. He watches you all the way to the stair. Behind you the array, for once, is quiet.

events.text: On the landing of floor {tw_floor} the war god is waiting for you, spearless, with a cup of terrible wine from his own heaven. "Taegwang of the Red Banner," he says. "I came to take this Tower for my pantheon. The door would not open to a god. It opened to a climber." He drinks. "So. I am a climber."

choices.text: Sit with him while he drinks

effects.log: It is very bad wine, he says, and finishes it alone while you keep him company. He tells you war stories, and in all of them, you notice, he is the one who stops first.

effects.log: He thinks a long time. "A hill," he says. "I won a hill and decided that was enough." He looks up the stairs. "It was not."

events.text: Floor {tw_floor} is the Dao of the Sword, and it is made of swords: hilts in the walls, blades in the floor, a ceiling of edges. You passed it. At the door the Dao itself speaks, plain as a sword is plain. "Put yours down," it says. "Then we will see what you are."

choices.text: Lay your weapon on the floor

effects.log: You lay it down. Nothing happens, for a long time. Then every blade in the room turns, very slightly, towards you, the way flowers turn to the sun.
"Good," says the Dao. "Most do." The door opens anyway. You are not sure whether you passed something or failed it.

choices.text: Lay it down, then pick it up again

choices.text: Answer with the Sword Dao you walk

effects.log: You answer in its own tongue. The ceiling of edges parts like a curtain, and the Dao bows its many blades to one of its own.

The Dao of Death is quiet a long time. "Being the last thing," it says at last, and lets you pass.

events.text: A stranger in a cloak stitched with silver stars sits on floor {tw_floor}, a hedge-witch from the other sky named Wenna Rook. She climbed from the western gate and reached the Daos, and they speak to her in a foreign tongue: her rites, her spells, her vows. She cannot understand yours, either.

choices.text: Teach her one word of qi

effects.log: You teach her "breath". She tries it. Her spell-light flickers, steadies, and turns, for a moment, the colour of jade. She stares at her hands.

choices.text: Ask her to show you a spell

effects.log: She speaks a word, and a small lamp of light hangs in the air between you. It does not use qi. You cannot see what it uses. It is beautiful.

choices.text: Sit and listen to the Daos speak to her

effects.log: You hear the Daos in her tongue: the same things, said differently. It is like hearing your own name in another accent.

events.text: Halfway across floor {tw_floor} every jade plaque in the hall stops turning, and the room goes silent in a way that has weight. Something very large is listening. Not speaking: listening. You understand that you may say one thing, and it will be heard.

choices.text: Ask why only the gifted may climb

effects.log: Your words go up and do not come back. The silence holds them for a long moment, as if turning them over. Then the plaques begin to turn again.
You do not know what for. The silence seems not to know either. But the light in the room warms, the way a face does.
You listen to the listening. For a breath, two things that are not used to being heard hear each other.

choices.text: Let it burn your strength for a while

choices.text: Look up at where it came from

effects.log: Nothing up there but cloud and nine drums. But you have the odd feeling that something looked back, and looked away first.

events.text: On floor {tw_floor} a woman in faded blue sits on a cloud step, wringing water from her sleeves. She is a goddess, or was: Wol-ha of the Seventh Spring, whose river dried and whose worshippers left. She is climbing the Tower to win back what she lost. The storm hit her harder than it hit you.

choices.text: Give her your hand up the next flight

effects.log: She takes it. Her hand is cold as a spring. At the top she says, "Gods do not say thank you," and then, quietly, says it.

choices.text: Ask what she will do with it, if she gets it back

effects.log: She thinks. "I do not know," she says. "That is why I am still climbing." She watches you go up ahead of her.

events.text: A big bearded man in oilcloth stands on floor {tw_floor}, a weather-warden from the other sky named Bram Hollis. Where he comes from, storms are spirits you bargain with. He tried to bargain with this one, and it laughed. He watched you stand under it instead. "Does that work?" he asks.

effects.log: He tries it, feet wide, chin down. The next bolt finds him standing. He roars with delight, half deafened. "No bargain at all!" he shouts.

choices.text: Ask him to teach you a bargain

effects.log: He teaches you a short rite of his people, a promise of bread to the wind. It is not qi. It works, a little, which bothers you.
